correctness.rationale: The finite core metric m is an exact complete diagram of the new tuple and hub. Every leaf-distance vector is admissible precisely by Katetov triangle inequalities. Any two different leaves are distance two; with distances in {1,2,3}, their triangles with each new point automatically hold, so choices factor as b(m)^n. With hub distances all two, tuple edge two is free, one forbids (1,3),(3,1), and three forbids only (1,1). A non-two hub coordinate removes at least a full third of assignments. These elementary restrictions prove the unique top base \(3^k\), the exactly-one-three-edge second base \(8\cdot3^{k-2}\), and the adjacent-two-three-edges third base \(22\cdot3^{k-3}\), with rigorous strictness for other possibilities. Counts and remainder follow. The packaged verifier independently brute-checks the first small arities and the k=2 exponential identity; its output ends ALL_TESTS_PASS.

value.rationale: Complete tuple-type/orbit counts are natural finite-parameter invariants of the universal homogeneous integer metric space. Rather than a single finite calculation, the theorem classifies the three largest exponential rates with exact coefficients at every fixed arity, identifying geometric meanings for dominant, one-defect and two-defect tuple cores. The equilateral concentration law has a sharp leading correction and supports further research on metric orbit growth and parameter-set geometry. The exact smaller coefficients remain algorithmically computable.
